content:
ID COLLISION, read first: this lessons-ledger record was allocated the id L-006, and RULES.md ALREADY uses "L-006" for a different thing — the witness gate ("every premise names its witness", adopted 2026-08-04 as a review gate rather than a lesson, per owner instruction). That label is cited across the park records and plan documents and was not renamed, because sweeping it would have touched many governing files. So: "L-006" in RULES.md, in docs/t011-*.md and in any park record means THE WITNESS GATE. "L-006" in the lessons ledger means the rule below. They are unrelated.

THE RULE. When ticket or plan text tells an implementer to branch on a value from a typed API, state the shape and the test, not just the field name: "reset.failed is a string[]; test failed.length > 0". A name alone lets an implementer write a branch that never fires (a wrong name reads undefined, which is falsy) or one that always fires (an empty array is truthy) — and neither produces a type error, a runtime error, or a failing test. After correcting one such clause, immediately audit its SIBLING clauses in the same entry: this failure comes in pairs.
context:
T-011's acceptanceAdditions.storeIntegration carried both failure directions at once, in adjacent clauses, and only one had been filed. ISS-073 (clause 6) named a GC field `noManifest` that does not exist — the shipped field is `noUsableManifest` (src/snapshot/store.ts:2961) — so code written from the ticket reads undefined and the branch silently never fires. Repairing it surfaced ISS-092 (clause 4), unfiled: the same entry called `reset.failed` a boolean hard stop, but it is `string[]` (store.ts:1197), so `if (reset.failed)` is truthy for the empty array and halts the bootstrap on every CLEAN reset — the store is never rebuilt and AC 1 fails with no test naming the cause. The governing plan had it right at :460 ("reset.failed non-empty"); the drift was ticket-versus-plan, in the direction that matters, since the ticket is the daily document.

Two reinforcements from the same 2026-08-05 pass. First, the correction itself must state a shape: a required-test row was written as `failed === []`, which is always false in JavaScript — the identical trap, inside the fix for it. Second, the same session's audit found the pattern one level up in the docs: a review-verified correction to ISS-065 replaced two stale grep counts but kept a characterization that depended on them, and the characterization was false (a publish test at tests-ts/snapshot-store.test.mjs:255 does plant a symlink at the commit target; the guard is simply shadowed by an earlier refusal). Correcting the number without re-deriving the sentence built on it is the same defect wearing different clothes.
title: [ID COLLISION: see note] Binding prose that names a typed value must state its SHAPE, not just its name
